appraisal_events.evidence: 'je sentis une fois de plus ma nullité intellectuelle et que je n'étais pas né pour la littérature'; 'Je me sentais consterné, réduit.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Having absorbed Norpois's harsh literary verdict, the narrator internalizes a crushing sense of his own intellectual worthlessness.

appraisal_events.evidence: Norpois recounts refusing to invite Bergotte to a Vienna reception without his mistress, calls his private life a 'degré d'ignominie,' and concludes 'au fond c'est un malade. C'est même sa seule excuse.'
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois extends his literary critique into a personal, moral diminishment of Bergotte, treating his private conduct as scandalous and pathological.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's self-assessment collapses under Norpois's judgment; he feels reduced and devoid of literary worth.
Norpois adds a moral and personal diminishment of Bergotte's private conduct on top of his earlier literary verdict.
